author: Diptanu Choudhury
text: We are seeing backlash against sandboxes for primarily a couple of reasons - vendors don't support users to overcommit compute. You can't pay for N cores and overcommit the number of sandboxes that are run on those cores. suggestedEngagement: This maps to how cloud overcommit made AWS viable — are sandbox vendors constrained architecturally or is isolation a hard requirement unique to agent workloads?
Curious what the failure mode looks like when an agent spikes compute mid-task — throttle, queue, or terminate? That seems like the crux of what vendors need to solve for enterprise reliability.
You shipped Nomad at HashiCorp at 1M containers — did container workloads show similarly bursty utilization patterns that made overcommit viable there?
